findings.quote: If you count allele combinations instead, only a heterozygous gene adds a choice.
findings.problem: The 'only' fails for a known exception that the lesson itself raises. Core Concept says 'A male's X and Y carry mostly different genes, so he has one allele of most genes on the X.' An X-linked gene in a male, such as $X^AY$, is not heterozygous (it has one allele, not a pair), yet it adds a choice: half his gametes carry $A$ on the X and half carry the Y with no allele for that gene. So a male $X^AY\,BB$ makes two allele combinations although no gene is heterozygous, and the rule as written gives one. Sex-linked crosses use exactly this gamete split (upcat-L140 names sex-linked inheritance, weak class, so no new case is required, but the stated rule must not be false). The round-3 fix itself is correct: the lesson now separates chromosome combinations ($4$ for $AaBB$ on two pairs) from allele combinations ($2$). Only the general 'only' clause breaks.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (test each 'only' against a known exception); the lesson's own Words for Genes section; OpenStax Biology 2e, 12.3 (X-linked traits: males are hemizygous and pass the X to daughters and the Y to sons).
